name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  test-js:
    name: JavaScript & TypeScript Suite (Node ${{ matrix.node-version }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node-version: [20.x, 22.x]

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Set up Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund

      - name: Build packages and bundles
        run: npm run build

      - name: Run test suites
        run: npm test

      - name: Verify npx three-live-cli (GitHub Release download without Rust)
        run: |
          npx --no-install three-live-cli --help
          npx --no-install three-live-cli --locate-only

      - name: Verify Docker & Debian (bookworm-slim + Glama trixie-slim) CLI compatibility
        if: matrix.node-version == '22.x'
        run: |
          BIN_PATH="$(node -e "console.log(JSON.parse(require('child_process').execFileSync('node', ['./bin/three-live-cli.js', '--locate-only'], {encoding: 'utf8'})).resolvedBinary)")"
          echo "Resolved release binary: ${BIN_PATH}"
          if objdump -T "${BIN_PATH}" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "GLIBC_"; then
            echo "::error::Prebuilt Linux CLI binary (${BIN_PATH}) dynamically links GLIBC symbols; expected static musl binary"
            exit 1
          fi
          docker run --rm -v "${BIN_PATH}:/usr/local/bin/three-live-cli:ro" debian:trixie-slim /usr/local/bin/three-live-cli --help > /dev/null
          docker build -t three-live-mcp .
          docker run --rm --entrypoint /usr/local/bin/three-live-cli three-live-mcp --help > /dev/null

  test-rust:
    name: Rust Compiler Suite (Ubuntu)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '20.x'

      - name: Build embedded JS engine asset
        run: |
          npm install --no-audit --no-fund
          npm run build

      - name: Set up Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@683b588c487a69d01f6c6ddf40f036ff682cc2c8 # master; stable toolchain below
        with:
          toolchain: stable
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - name: Rustfmt check
        run: cargo fmt --manifest-path compiler/Cargo.toml -- --check

      - name: Cargo check (default & JNI features)
        run: |
          cargo check --manifest-path compiler/Cargo.toml --all-targets
          cargo check --manifest-path compiler/Cargo.toml --features jni

      # The debug profile is the primary gate: it is the only one where `overflow-checks`
      # and `debug_assert!` are live, which matters for a crate doing offset and size
      # arithmetic over untrusted input.
      - name: Run compiler unit tests (debug, with JNI)
        run: cargo test --manifest-path compiler/Cargo.toml --features jni -- --test-threads=1

      # Release must also be tested, because several behaviours exist *only* in this profile:
      #   * `panic = "unwind"` is set in `[profile.release]` alone, so every `catch_unwind`
      #     FFI/JNI firewall in lib.rs, ffi.rs and jni.rs is exercised by nothing otherwise.
      #   * `lto`, `codegen-units = 1` and `opt-level = 3` are release-only, and this crate
      #     has `unsafe` FFI, so optimizer-sensitive bugs surface nowhere else.
      #   * The SECURITY_3D_*_CEILING_MS release values are the real product constraints;
      #     their debug counterparts are far too loose to act as regression tripwires.
      #   * It is what actually ships in the AAR, the xcframework and the wasm bundle.
      # Runtime is ~2s; the cost is the LTO build, and the release CLI build below reuses it.
      - name: Run compiler unit tests (release, with JNI)
        run: cargo test --manifest-path compiler/Cargo.toml --features jni --release -- --test-threads=1

      - name: Build release CLI binary
        run: cargo build --manifest-path compiler/Cargo.toml --release --bin three-live-cli

      - name: Verify npx three-live-cli (local release binary discovery)
        run: |
          npx --no-install three-live-cli --locate-only
          npx --no-install three-live-cli --help

  test-android:
    name: Android Library Suite (Ubuntu, Java 17)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Set up Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@cf277c60eb25467037889841efdb72551f06f6c3 # v4
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'

      # gradle-version must be set explicitly. setup-gradle defaults to 'wrapper', and
      # gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar is deliberately not checked in, so without this the
      # steps below would silently fall back to whatever Gradle the runner image happens to ship.
      # Keep in sync with gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties.
      - name: Set up Gradle
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@d9c87d481d55275bb5441eef3fe0e46805f9ef70 # v3
        with:
          gradle-version: '8.7'

      - name: Run Android unit tests
        run: gradle :mobile:android:testReleaseUnitTest :mobile:android-filament:testReleaseUnitTest :mobile:android-firebase-ai:testReleaseUnitTest :mobile:android-detect-mlkit:testReleaseUnitTest :mobile:android-hands-androidxr:testReleaseUnitTest :mobile:android-hands-mediapipe:testReleaseUnitTest --stacktrace

      - name: Assemble Android release AARs (core + optional Filament / Firebase AI / ML Kit / Hands modules)
        run: gradle :mobile:android:assembleRelease :mobile:android-filament:assembleRelease :mobile:android-firebase-ai:assembleRelease :mobile:android-detect-mlkit:assembleRelease :mobile:android-hands-androidxr:assembleRelease :mobile:android-hands-mediapipe:assembleRelease --stacktrace

      # The example app is not shipped, but it is the first thing a new user runs, and it is the
      # only consumer of the library's public API. Compiling it here is what catches breakage in
      # the Filament integration (and in our own API surface) before it reaches HEAD.
      - name: Assemble Compose example app
        run: gradle :mobile:examples:android_compose:assembleRelease --stacktrace

  test-swift:
    name: Swift Package & iOS Example Suite (macOS)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      # The SwiftPM target needs its own copy of the C header. A divergence between the two
      # copies is an ABI bug that no compiler would catch, so assert they are identical.
      - name: Check C header is in sync
        run: bash scripts/sync_c_header.sh --check

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '20.x'

      - name: Build embedded JS engine asset
        run: |
          npm install --no-audit --no-fund
          npm run build

      - name: Set up Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@683b588c487a69d01f6c6ddf40f036ff682cc2c8 # master; stable toolchain below
        with:
          toolchain: stable
          targets: aarch64-apple-ios, aarch64-apple-ios-sim, x86_64-apple-ios, aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin

      - name: Build XCFramework
        run: bash scripts/build_ios_xcframework.sh

      # Deliberately uses the root manifest with no --package-path. This is the manifest
      # every external consumer resolves, so it is the one CI must exercise.
      - name: Build Swift package
        run: swift build

      - name: Run Swift package tests
        run: swift test

      # `swift build` only covers the macOS host, where `canImport(UIKit)` is false and the
      # whole of QuickLookHelper.swift is preprocessed away. These steps are what actually
      # type-check the iOS-only and visionOS-only code paths.
      - name: Compile for iOS
        run: |
          xcodebuild -scheme ThreeLiveCompiler \
            -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
            -derivedDataPath .build/xcodebuild-ios \
            build

      - name: Compile for visionOS
        run: |
          if [ -d mobile/ios/ThreeLiveCompiler.xcframework/xros-arm64 ] && xcodebuild -showsdks | grep -q -- '-sdk xros'; then
            xcodebuild -scheme ThreeLiveCompiler \
              -destination 'generic/platform=visionOS' \
              -derivedDataPath .build/xcodebuild-visionos \
              build
          else
            echo "::warning::visionOS XCFramework slice or SDK unavailable on this runner; skipping visionOS compile check"
          fi

      - name: Compile for tvOS
        run: |
          if [ -d mobile/ios/ThreeLiveCompiler.xcframework/tvos-arm64 ] && xcodebuild -showsdks | grep -q -- '-sdk appletvos'; then
            xcodebuild -scheme ThreeLiveCompiler \
              -destination 'generic/platform=tvOS' \
              -derivedDataPath .build/xcodebuild-tvos \
              build
          else
            echo "::warning::tvOS XCFramework slice or SDK unavailable on this runner; skipping tvOS compile check"
          fi

      - name: Install XcodeGen
        run: brew install xcodegen

      - name: Generate and build iOS example app
        working-directory: mobile/examples/ios_swiftui
        run: |
          xcodegen generate
          xcodebuild -project ThreeLiveDemo.xcodeproj \
            -scheme ThreeLiveDemo \
            -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
            -derivedDataPath .build/xcodebuild \
            CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
            build

      - name: Check release checksum pin
        run: |
          if grep -q '^let releaseChecksum = "0\{64\}"$' Package.swift; then
            echo "::warning::Package.swift still carries the placeholder release checksum. \
            This is expected before the first release; the release workflow pins it via \
            scripts/update_spm_binary_target.sh."
          else
            echo "Release checksum is pinned."
          fi

# Three-Live Android Live Compiler & AR Studio (Jetpack Compose + Google Filament + ARCore)

A complete, turnkey native Android sample application demonstrating on-device
compilation of Three.js JavaScript into binary glTF 2.0 (GLB) with zero memory
copies, rendered interactively using Google Filament in 3D and Google ARCore
Scene Viewer in AR.

## Features

- **Live Code Editor**: Interactive Jetpack Compose monospace text area allowing developers to write, edit, or paste arbitrary Three.js scene scripts directly on Android devices.
-   **Unified Preset Gallery**: One-tap scene presets matching Web and iOS
    (`Quantum Core`, `Torus Knot`, `Emerald Crystal`, `Orbital Spheres`).
- **Sub-Millisecond Rust Compiler**: Embedded `libthree_live_compiler.so` compiled via Rust NDK.
- **Zero-Copy JNI Buffer**: Allocates `.glb` wire bytes in native Rust memory and maps directly to a Java `DirectByteBuffer` (`GlbBuffer`), eliminating GC memory pressure and copies.
- **Google Filament 3D Viewport**: Real-time PBR rendering with camera orbit and dynamic lighting.
-   **Google ARCore Scene Viewer (`View in AR`)**: Exports the compiled GLB via
    `FileProvider` (`SceneViewerHelper.kt`) and launches full-screen Google
    ARCore Scene Viewer (`ar_preferred` mode) to place models onto real-world
    surfaces.

## Quickstart

### 1. Build the Native Compiler AAR

From repository root:

```bash
bash scripts/build_android_aar.sh
```

### 2. Open in Android Studio

1. Open Android Studio (Hedgehog or newer).
2. Select **Open** and choose `mobile/examples/android_compose`.
3. Sync Gradle and click **Run** (on physical device or x86_64 emulator with GLES 3.0+).

# LLM & Agent Authoring Guide (`three-live` & `xr-live`)

This guide is designed for **LLMs, coding assistants, and autonomous agents**
generating 3D and Spatial Computing (AR/VR/XR) code with `<three-live>` and
`<xr-live>`.

- **Repository Agent Instructions:** [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md)
- **Installable Agent Skills:**
  - [`skills/three-live-authoring/SKILL.md`](../skills/three-live-authoring/SKILL.md) (building 3D/XR scenes and apps)
  - [`skills/xr-live-plugin-dev/SKILL.md`](../skills/xr-live-plugin-dev/SKILL.md) (contributing cross-platform traits and plugins)
- **Single-File Context Feeds:** [`/llms.txt`](../llms.txt) (concise index) and [`/llms-full.txt`](../llms-full.txt) (complete reference)

You can copy the **System Prompt Snippet** below directly into any LLM prompt or
agent skill to guarantee valid, zero-hallucination output.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Copy-Paste System Prompt Snippet for LLMs

```markdown
You are authoring 3D and Spatial Computing scenes using Google's `three-live` and `xr-live` web components.

### 1. Choose the Right Component & Bundle
- Use `<three-live>` (`three-live.min.js` or `three-live-full.min.js`) for 3D product viewers, procedural Three.js scenes, `KHR_interactivity` behavior graphs, PBR Next materials, and 1-tap mobile AR handoff (Quick Look / Scene Viewer / WebXR).
- Use `<xr-live>` (`xr-live.min.js` or `xr-live-full.min.js`) when the scene requires interactive 6DoF WebXR, declarative spatial traits (`userData.xr`), spatial HTML cards (`<div slot="spatial">`), depth occlusion & physics (`xr-depth`), 25-joint hand tracking (`xr-hands`), any of the 15 spatial plugins (`head-follow`, `manipulation-handles`, `world-understanding`, `gemini-live`, `spatial-paint`, `depth-particles`, `splat-loader`, `spatial-measure`, `magnetic-snap`, `gaze-dwell`, `exploded-view`, `persistent-anchors`, `spatial-locomotion`, `shared-room`, `spatial-audio`), or any of the 6 `xr-live-sim` simulation plugins (`character-controller`, `steering-agents`, `rigid-body`, `hit-zones`, `objectives`, `synth-audio`; available in `xr-live-sim.min.js` and `xr-live-full.min.js`).

### 2. Procedural `<script type="text/three">` Rules
- Inside `<script type="text/three">`, the globals `THREE` and `scene` (a `THREE.Scene` instance) are pre-defined.
- ALWAYS add the `allow-client-scripts` attribute to any `<three-live>` or `<xr-live>` element that contains an inline `<script type="text/three">`; without it the script is refused and nothing renders.
- Add all meshes, groups, and lights directly to `scene.add(...)`, and give interactive meshes a unique `mesh.name = '...'`.
- Attach canonical spatial traits via `mesh.userData.xr = { ... }`:
  - `grab`: `'1-hand' | '2-hand' | true`
  - `scale`: `{ min: 0.1, max: 5.0 } | true`
  - `billboard`: `'capsule' | 'cylindrical' | 'spherical' | true`
  - `follow`: `'head' | 'hand-left' | 'hand-right'` or `{ mode: 'head', lazy: true, distance: 1.2, deadzoneDeg: 15, stiffness: 6, height: -0.1, faceUser: true }`
  - `anchor`: `'floor' | 'wall' | 'ceiling' | 'table' | 'horizontal' | 'vertical'` or `{ target: 'table', id: 'part-1', persist: true }`
  - `physics` / `rigidBody`: `'dynamic' | 'static' | 'kinematic' | true` or `{ body: 'dynamic' | 'static' | 'kinematic', shape: 'auto' | 'box' | 'sphere' | 'cylinder', mass: 1, restitution: 0.35, friction: 0.5, linearDamping: 0.05, angularDamping: 0.1, gravityScale: 1, velocity: [0, 0, 0], angularVelocity: [0, 0, 0], lockRotation: false }`
  - `joint`: `'hinge' | 'slider' | 'spring' | 'ball' | true` or `{ type: 'hinge' | 'slider' | 'spring' | 'ball', target: 'nodeName' | 'world', anchor: [0, 0, 0], axis: 'x' | 'y' | 'z' | [0, 1, 0], limits: [-45, 90], stiffness: 40, damping: 4, restLength: 0.5, motorSpeed: 0, motorMaxForce: 10 }`
  - `orbit`: `{ target: [x, y, z] | 'nodeName', radius: 0.5, speed: 0.8, height: 0, faceCenter: true }`
  - `handles`: `{ rotateAxis: 'y' | 'none', minScale: 0.2, maxScale: 3.0 } | true`
  - `dimensions`: `{ unit: 'auto' | 'm' | 'cm' | 'mm' | 'in' | 'ft-in', axes: ['x', 'y', 'z'], color: '#38bdf8', showOnSelect: false } | true`
  - `snapTo`: `{ grid: 0.05, angleDeg: 15, surface: 'floor' | 'wall' | 'ceiling' | 'any' | 'none', socketTag: 'dock', radius: 0.15 } | true`
  - `snapSocket`: `'dock'` or `{ tag: 'dock', radius: 0.15, alignRotation: true, highlightColor: '#22c55e' }`
  - `gaze`: `{ dwellMs: 1200, action: 'select' | 'ask', repeat: false } | true`
  - `explode`: `{ direction: [0, 1, 0], distance: 0.35, layer: 1, leaderLine: true } | boolean`
  - `navigable`: `true | 'walkable' | 'blocked'`
  - `sync`: `boolean` (multi-user `shared-room` transform sync; defaults to `true` on grabbable nodes)
  - `particles`: `{ preset: 'rain' | 'snow' | 'sparks' | 'confetti', count: 400, area: [2, 2, 2], speed: 1.0 }`
  - `holdToAsk`: `{ prompt: 'What is this?', holdMs: 600 } | true`
  - `worldUnderstanding`: `{ planes: true, meshes: false, reticle: true }`
  - `splatUrl`: `'https://.../capture.spz'` (or `.splat`)
  - `splat`: `{ url: 'https://.../capture.spz', shDegree: 3, maxSplats: 500000 }`
  - `bloom`: `{ strength: 1.2, threshold: 0.8, radius: 0.5 } | boolean | number`
  - `outline`: `{ color: '#38bdf8', thickness: 0.03 } | boolean | string`
  - `ik`: `{ root: 'RootNode', mid: 'MidNode', effector: 'EffectorNode', target: 'TargetNodeName' | [x, y, z], pole: 'PoleNodeName' | [x, y, z], solver: 'two-bone' | 'fabrik', iterations: 10, tolerance: 0.001, weight: 1 }`
  - `lod`: `true` or `[0, 5, 12]` or `{ distances: [0, 5, 12], ratios: [1.0, 0.4, 0.15], cullDistance: 30, hysteresis: 0.05 }` (also `new THREE.LOD()` with `.addLevel(obj, distance)`)
  - `text`: `{ text: '3D Label', size: 0.2, depth: 0.04, bevelEnabled: true }`
  - `audioEmitter` / `audio`: `'hum'` or `{ preset: 'hum' | 'reactor' | 'wind' | 'beacon' | 'geiger' | 'chimeLoop' | 'machinery' | 'water' | 'confirm', src: 'https://.../sound.mp3', volume: 0.7, loop: true, autoplay: true, playOnSelect: false, distanceModel: 'inverse' | 'linear' | 'exponential', refDistance: 1.0, maxDistance: 20.0, rolloffFactor: 1.0, coneInnerAngle: 360, coneOuterAngle: 360, coneOuterGain: 0, pitchHz: 440 }`
  - `character`: `true` or `{ mode: 'third-person' | 'first-person' | 'top-down' | 'fixed-camera', speed: 4, jumpVelocity: 5.5, gravity: 15, radius: 0.35, height: 1.7, cameraDistance: 3.5, cameraHeight: 1.6 }`
  - `agent`: `'patrol'` or `{ behavior: 'patrol' | 'chase' | 'flee' | 'follow' | 'wander', speed: 2.5, waypoints: [[x, y, z], ...], loop: true, sightDistance: 8, sightAngleDeg: 110, reachDistance: 0.6, target: 'character' | 'nodeName', alertBehavior: 'chase' }`
  - `integrity`: `100` or `{ max: 100, current: 100, group: 'hazard' | 'player' | 'prop', scoreValue: 25, removeOnDeplete: true, hitCooldownMs: 120, contactAmount: 25 }`
  - `zone`: `{ shape: 'box' | 'sphere' | 'cylinder', size: [2, 2, 2], radius: 1.5, height: 2, triggerGroup: 'player', action: 'checkpoint' | 'hazard' | 'complete' | 'fail' | 'event', ratePerSec: 20, once: false, color: '#22c55e' }`
  - `spawner`: `{ template: 'BotNode', intervalSec: 3, maxActive: 5, maxTotal: 15, radius: 1.5, autoStart: true }`
  - `objective`: `'Inspect valve'` or `{ id: 'valve-1', label: 'Inspect valve', type: 'reach' | 'clear' | 'collect' | 'activate' | 'hold', points: 50, order: 1, required: true, holdSec: 1.5, reachRadius: 1.2 }`
  - `audioCues`: `{ onHit: 'thud', onDeplete: 'buzz', onCollect: 'chime', onObjective: 'beep', onJump: 'whoosh', onScenarioPass: 'sweep', onScenarioFail: 'alarm', pitchHz: 440, gain: 0.7 }`
- Attach declarative `KHR_interactivity` behaviors via `mesh.userData.interactivity = { onSelect: [...], onHoverIn: [...], onStart: [...] }` using actions `toggleTransform`, `interpolate`, `setProperty`, `toggleVisibility`, `cycleMaterialColor`, `playAnimation`, `stopAnimation`, or `sendEvent`.
- NEVER use `GLTFLoader`, `OBJLoader`, `TextureLoader`, `EffectComposer`, `ShaderMaterial`, `RawShaderMaterial`, or `requestAnimationFrame` inside `<script type="text/three">`.
- NEVER create a `THREE.WebGLRenderer` or attach DOM canvas elements inside `<script type="text/three">`.
- Respect strict scene quotas: max 1,000 meshes, 100,000 vertices, 300,000 indices, 16 textures, 3-second execution timeout.

### 3. Allowed `THREE.*` Constructors inside `<script type="text/three">`
- Math & IK: `Vector2`, `Vector3`, `Vector4`, `Euler`, `Quaternion`, `Matrix3`, `Matrix4`, `Color`, `MathUtils`, `Clock`, `IKSolver` (`solveTwoBone`, `solveFABRIK`)
```

### Permissive Fallback Shims & Diagnostic Warnings (JS & Rust Compiler)

While LLMs should prefer the canonical APIs above for highest fidelity, both the
JavaScript authoring runtime (`three-author`) and the native Rust compiler
(`compiler/`) include **permissive fallback shims** so common LLM-generated
Three.js assumptions never crash or abort a 3D/XR scene:

-   **Shaders (`ShaderMaterial`, `RawShaderMaterial`):** Gracefully downgraded
    to `MeshStandardMaterial`, preserving `uniforms.color.value` /
    `params.color` and opacity so the mesh renders in 3D and XR.
-   **Polyhedra & Extended Geometries (`IcosahedronGeometry`,
    `OctahedronGeometry`, `DodecahedronGeometry`, `TetrahedronGeometry`,
    `CapsuleGeometry`, `RingGeometry`, `CircleGeometry`):** Mapped to
    parameter-compatible `SphereGeometry` or `CylinderGeometry` primitives.
-   **Lights (`SpotLight`, `HemisphereLight`, `RectAreaLight`):** Mapped to
    `PointLight` or `AmbientLight`.
-   **Unknown / Hallucinated Classes:** Any unknown `THREE.*` class resolves to
    a safe recursive no-op proxy, and `new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat)` automatically
    substitutes a fallback `BoxGeometry` / `MeshStandardMaterial` if passed a
    non-geometry or non-material proxy.
-   **Browser Boilerplate (`requestAnimationFrame`, `window`, `document`):**
    Safely shimmed in headless/Worker/Rust sandboxes so trailing render loops
    (`requestAnimationFrame(animate)`) or `window.innerWidth /
    window.innerHeight` checks do not throw `ReferenceError`.
-   **Diagnostic Warnings:** Every degraded feature logs a deduplicated
    `console.warn` and is recorded in `THREE.getAuthorWarnings()` (reset via
    `THREE.clearAuthorWarnings()`).

## 5. Closed-Loop AI Agent Verification (`three-live-cli` & MCP Server)

AI coding agents can validate, visually inspect, and simulate
`<script type="text/three">` scenes, `.html` host documents, and `.glb` files in
under `50 ms` without launching a headless browser—either via CLI subcommands or
via the built-in **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** stdio server
(`three-live-cli mcp`):

```bash
# Register the MCP stdio server in Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, or Windsurf:
claude mcp add three-live -- npx -y -p three-live three-live-cli mcp
```

Or add to `.mcp.json` / `claude_desktop_config.json` / `.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "three-live": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "-p", "three-live", "three-live-cli", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

The MCP server exposes 10 tools (`three_live_validate`, `three_live_render`,
`three_live_convert`, `three_live_sim`, `three_live_link`,
`three_live_gym_reset`, `three_live_gym_step`, `three_live_gym_close`,
`three_live_from_image`, `three_live_bake_textures`), 1 resource
(`three-live://docs/authoring-guide`), and 2 prompts (`author_three_live_scene`,
`build_from_reference`). Note that `three_live_render` returns MCP `image/png`
content blocks directly into multimodal LLM context so agents can visually
self-correct camera framing, overlap, and lighting.

### AI Textures (`three_live_bake_textures`)

`mesh.userData.xr = { material: { preset: 'brick', prompt: '…' } }` asks for an
AI texture; until a texture pack has it, the preset is shown. Get the geometry
and presets right first. Then, only if the user wants photoreal surfaces and an
image endpoint is configured (`THREE_LIVE_AI_IMAGE_ENDPOINT`), call
`three_live_bake_textures` with `outputPath: 'scene.textures.json'`. It returns
a preset-vs-AI comparison image. Pass `texturePackPath` to `three_live_render`,
`three_live_convert`, `three_live_validate`, or `three_live_sim` to see or
export the textured scene. On the command line:

```bash
$ npx three-live-cli textures bake scene.js -o scene.textures.json --glb scene.glb
$ npx three-live-cli render scene.js --texture-pack scene.textures.json -o textured.png
```

### Reference-Driven Authoring (`reference`)

When the user supplies a photo, product shot, design mockup, sketch, or CAD
blueprint, pass it to `three_live_render` as `reference` (a local PNG/JPEG path
or a `data:image/...;base64,` URI; remote URLs are never fetched):

```json
{ "name": "three_live_render",
  "arguments": { "inputPath": "lamp.js", "reference": "lamp_photo.jpg", "view": "camera" } }
```

-   The scene renders at the reference's aspect ratio into a **REFERENCE |
    RENDER | OVERLAY | SILHOUETTE DIFF** sheet. On plain or transparent
    backgrounds the OVERLAY is auto-aligned for position and scale, and the DIFF
    panel marks render-only areas orange and reference-only areas cyan.
-   The JSON `reference` block reports `silhouetteIou` (scale/translation
    invariant), `referenceAspect` / `renderAspect` / `aspectError`,
    `silhouetteReliable`, and `guidance`. Aim for `silhouetteIou >= 0.85` and
    `|aspectError| < 0.05` when `silhouetteReliable` is true; for busy photo
    backgrounds or line-art sketches, judge by the OVERLAY panel.
-   Use `view: "front" | "right" | "top"` for orthographic blueprints and
    `view: "camera"` (default) for perspective photos, tuning `cameraPosition`,
    `cameraTarget`, and `cameraFov` to match the photo's perspective.
-   JPEG EXIF orientation is honored; PNG supports every color type, bit depth,
    transparency, and Adam7 interlacing.

You can also invoke the CLI directly from shell tools:

```bash

three-live-cli validate scene.js --json

# 2. 4-Up Quad Contact Sheet (Perspective + Front + Right + Top with 1m Grid & AABB Labels)

# 3. Multi-Frame Temporal Filmstrip or Animated GIF89a (`animate(t)` + KHR_interactivity Tweens)
three-live-cli render scene.js -o anim.png --frames=4 --duration=2.0 --trigger-select=crystal

# 4. Deterministic 60Hz Scenario & KHR_interactivity Simulation
three-live-cli sim scene.js --duration=5.0 \
  --actions='[{"at":0.2,"type":"select","target":"crystal"},{"at":0.5,"type":"moveCharacter","direction":[0,0,-1],"duration":1.5,"jump":true}]' \
```

### Agent Gym: Play a Scene Step by Step (`three_live_gym_reset` / `three_live_gym_step`)

`three_live_sim` runs a script you write up front. The gym lets an agent *play*
a scene instead: act, look at the result, and decide the next action. Use it to
check that a level is winnable, tune enemy speed or jump heights, or test
interactive scenes end to end.

"Gym" is the reinforcement-learning name for this kind of playable environment,
after OpenAI Gym (now Gymnasium): `reset` starts an episode, and each `step`
takes actions and returns an observation, a reward, and whether the episode is
done. No machine learning is involved; any agent (or script) that can call a
tool in a loop can use it.

```json
{ "name": "three_live_gym_reset",
  "arguments": { "inputPath": "level.js", "watch": ["Hero", "Coin"] } }
// -> { "sessionId": "gym-1", "tick": 0, "scenarioState": "running", "bodies": [...] }

{ "name": "three_live_gym_step",
  "arguments": { "sessionId": "gym-1", "ticks": 30,
                 "actions": [{ "type": "moveCharacter", "direction": [0, 0, -1], "jump": true }] } }
// -> { "tick": 30, "reward": 5, "events": ["objectiveComplete:Coin"],
//      "newObjectives": ["Coin"], "done": true, "scenarioState": "victory", ... }
```

-   Each step applies `actions` (same shapes as `three_live_sim`; `at` is a
    delay in seconds from the start of the step) and advances `ticks` 60 Hz
    ticks (default 30, max 600). `moveCharacter` lasts the whole step unless you
    pass `duration`.
-   Every observation lists `bodies` (position, rotation, scale, visible,
    grounded, health, destroyed; at most 64, use `watch` to choose), `score`,
    `reward` (score gained this step), and the `events`, `audioCues`, and
    `newObjectives` fired during the step.
-   `done` turns true on `victory` (all `required: true` objectives done), on
    `defeat` (the character is destroyed), or at the 120 s / 240-step limit.
    Further steps fail; call `three_live_gym_reset` again.
-   Pass `includeFrame: true` (with `view`, `width`, `height`) to get a PNG of
    the state after the step.
-   The reset observation lists the `events` and `audioCues` fired at `t = 0`
    (`onSpawn`, `onStart`, trait registrations).
-   Episodes are deterministic: the same actions always give the same
    observations. Steps on static scenes take well under a millisecond; scenes
    with `animate(t)` or `requestAnimationFrame` re-run their script once per
    step (tens of milliseconds for typical scenes). Close sessions you are done
    with (`three_live_gym_close`); beyond 16 the least recently used is evicted.

Without MCP, use `three-live-cli gym`. One command per step suits shell-tool
agents; the session file holds the scene and every step, and each call replays
it deterministically:

```bash
three-live-cli gym reset level.js --session ep.json --watch Hero,Coin
three-live-cli gym step --session ep.json --ticks 30 \
  --actions '[{"type":"moveCharacter","direction":[0,0,-1]}]' --frame step.png
```

For scripts and RL harnesses, `three-live-cli gym play level.js` prints the
`t = 0` observation, then reads one JSON step per stdin line
(`{"actions": [...], "ticks": 30, "frame": "f.png"}`) and prints one observation
(or `{"error": ...}`) per line, keeping state in memory.

name: Deploy Playgrounds to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: "pages"
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build-site:
    name: Build Playgrounds & Web Bundles
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      pages_enabled: ${{ steps.check_pages.outputs.enabled }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '20.x'

      - name: Install dependencies and build bundles
        run: |
          npm install --no-audit --no-fund
          npm run build

      - name: Assemble static site (playgrounds + /dist/ bundles)
        run: |
          rm -rf _site
          mkdir -p _site/dist
          cp -R examples/* _site/
          cp dist/*.js dist/*.min.js dist/three-live-sandbox.html _site/dist/
          cp three-live/dist/*.min.js _site/dist/
          cp xr-live/dist/*.js xr-live/dist/*.min.js _site/dist/
          touch _site/.nojekyll
          ls -la _site _site/three _site/xr _site/dist

      - name: Check whether GitHub Pages is enabled for this repository
        id: check_pages
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pages" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "GitHub Pages is enabled."
            echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "::notice::GitHub Pages is not enabled yet (or repository is still private). Built site artifact successfully; enable Pages (Source: GitHub Actions) in repository settings once public."
            echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Configure Pages
        if: steps.check_pages.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        uses: actions/configure-pages@983d7736d9b0ae728b81ab479565c72886d7745b # v5

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@56afc609e74202658d3ffba0e8f6dda462b719fa # v3
        with:
          path: _site

  deploy-site:
    name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
    if: needs.build-site.outputs.pages_enabled == 'true'
    needs: build-site
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@d6db90164ac5ed86f2b6aed7e0febac5b3c0c03e # v4

name: Release & Publish

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build-binaries:
    name: Build Native CLI Binaries (${{ matrix.target }})
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            os: ubuntu-latest
            artifact_name: three-live-cli-linux-x86_64
          - target: aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
            os: ubuntu-latest
            artifact_name: three-live-cli-linux-aarch64
          - target: x86_64-apple-darwin
            os: macos-latest
            artifact_name: three-live-cli-macos-x86_64
          - target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            os: macos-latest
            artifact_name: three-live-cli-macos-arm64
          - target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
            os: windows-latest
            artifact_name: three-live-cli-windows-x86_64.exe

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '20.x'

      - name: Build embedded JS engine asset
        run: |
          npm install --no-audit --no-fund
          npm run build

      - name: Set up Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@683b588c487a69d01f6c6ddf40f036ff682cc2c8 # master; stable toolchain below
        with:
          toolchain: stable
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Build with Cargo
        env:
          CARGO_TARGET_AARCH64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_MUSL_LINKER: rust-lld
        run: cargo build --manifest-path compiler/Cargo.toml --release --bin three-live-cli --target ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Verify Linux binary is statically linked (zero GLIBC version dependency)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          file "target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/three-live-cli"
          if objdump -T "target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/three-live-cli" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "GLIBC_"; then
            echo "::error::Linux CLI binary contains dynamic GLIBC symbol references; expected static musl binary"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Rename binary to target artifact name
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ -f "target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/three-live-cli.exe" ]; then
            cp "target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/three-live-cli.exe" "target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/${{ matrix.artifact_name }}"
          else
            cp "target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/three-live-cli" "target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/${{ matrix.artifact_name }}"
          fi

      - name: Upload Binary Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.artifact_name }}
          path: target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/${{ matrix.artifact_name }}
          if-no-files-found: error

  build-android:
    name: Build Android AAR
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '20.x'

      - name: Build embedded JS engine asset
        run: |
          npm install --no-audit --no-fund
          npm run build

      - name: Set up Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@cf277c60eb25467037889841efdb72551f06f6c3 # v4
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'

      # Keep in sync with gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties; see the note in ci.yml.
      - name: Set up Gradle
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@d9c87d481d55275bb5441eef3fe0e46805f9ef70 # v3
        with:
          gradle-version: '8.7'

      - name: Set up Android NDK
        id: setup-ndk
        uses: nttld/setup-ndk@ed92fe6cadad69be94a966a7ee3271275e62f779 # v1
        with:
          ndk-version: r26b

      - name: Set up Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@683b588c487a69d01f6c6ddf40f036ff682cc2c8 # master; stable toolchain below
        with:
          toolchain: stable
          targets: aarch64-linux-android, x86_64-linux-android, armv7-linux-androideabi

      - name: Install cargo-ndk
        run: cargo install cargo-ndk

      - name: Build Android AAR
        run: bash scripts/build_android_aar.sh
        env:
          ANDROID_NDK_HOME: ${{ steps.setup-ndk.outputs.ndk-path }}

      # Guard against shipping a Java-only AAR: without the cross-compiled .so files every
      # ThreeCompiler call throws UnsatisfiedLinkError at runtime.
      - name: Verify AAR contains native libraries
        run: |
          aar=$(ls mobile/android/build/outputs/aar/*-release.aar)
          echo "Inspecting ${aar}"
          for abi in arm64-v8a armeabi-v7a x86_64; do
            unzip -l "${aar}" | grep -q "jni/${abi}/libthree_live_compiler.so" \
              || { echo "::error::AAR is missing jni/${abi}/libthree_live_compiler.so"; exit 1; }
          done
          echo "All three ABIs present."

      # if-no-files-found defaults to 'warn', which previously let this job go green while
      # uploading nothing at all.
      - name: Upload Android AAR Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: three-live-compiler-release-aar
          path: mobile/android/build/outputs/aar/*-release.aar
          if-no-files-found: error

      # Optional Android adapter modules are pure Kotlin on top of the core AAR.
      - name: Build optional Android adapter AARs
        run: >
          gradle
          :mobile:android-filament:assembleRelease
          :mobile:android-firebase-ai:assembleRelease
          :mobile:android-detect-mlkit:assembleRelease
          :mobile:android-hands-androidxr:assembleRelease
          :mobile:android-hands-mediapipe:assembleRelease
          --stacktrace

      - name: Upload Filament renderer AAR Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: three-live-filament-release-aar
          path: mobile/android-filament/build/outputs/aar/*-release.aar
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Upload Firebase AI adapter AAR Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: three-live-firebase-ai-release-aar
          path: mobile/android-firebase-ai/build/outputs/aar/*-release.aar
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Upload ML Kit detector AAR Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: three-live-detect-mlkit-release-aar
          path: mobile/android-detect-mlkit/build/outputs/aar/*-release.aar
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Upload Android XR hands AAR Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: three-live-hands-androidxr-release-aar
          path: mobile/android-hands-androidxr/build/outputs/aar/*-release.aar
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Upload MediaPipe hands AAR Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: three-live-hands-mediapipe-release-aar
          path: mobile/android-hands-mediapipe/build/outputs/aar/*-release.aar
          if-no-files-found: error

      # Always validate POMs and publication wiring against mavenLocal, publish to GitHub Packages
      # Maven using GITHUB_TOKEN, and publish to Maven Central if Sonatype credentials are set.
      - name: Publish Android AARs to Maven Local
        run: >
          gradle
          :mobile:android:publishReleasePublicationToMavenLocal
          :mobile:android-filament:publishReleasePublicationToMavenLocal
          :mobile:android-firebase-ai:publishReleasePublicationToMavenLocal
          :mobile:android-detect-mlkit:publishReleasePublicationToMavenLocal
          :mobile:android-hands-androidxr:publishReleasePublicationToMavenLocal
          :mobile:android-hands-mediapipe:publishReleasePublicationToMavenLocal
          --stacktrace

      - name: Publish Android AARs to GitHub Packages Maven
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GITHUB_ACTOR: ${{ github.actor }}
          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          gradle \
            :mobile:android:publishReleasePublicationToGitHubPackagesRepository \
            :mobile:android-filament:publishReleasePublicationToGitHubPackagesRepository \
            :mobile:android-firebase-ai:publishReleasePublicationToGitHubPackagesRepository \
            :mobile:android-detect-mlkit:publishReleasePublicationToGitHubPackagesRepository \
            :mobile:android-hands-androidxr:publishReleasePublicationToGitHubPackagesRepository \
            :mobile:android-hands-mediapipe:publishReleasePublicationToGitHubPackagesRepository \
            --stacktrace || echo "::notice::GitHub Packages Maven publish skipped or version already exists."

      - name: Publish Android AARs to Maven Central
        env:
          MAVEN_CENTRAL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.MAVEN_CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
          MAVEN_CENTRAL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MAVEN_CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
          MAVEN_CENTRAL_REPO_URL: ${{ secrets.MAVEN_CENTRAL_REPO_URL }}
          MAVEN_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.MAVEN_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "${MAVEN_CENTRAL_USERNAME:-}" ] || [ -z "${MAVEN_CENTRAL_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::MAVEN_CENTRAL_USERNAME / MAVEN_CENTRAL_PASSWORD secrets are not configured yet; skipping Maven Central publish."
            exit 0
          fi
          gradle \
            :mobile:android:publishReleasePublicationToMavenCentralRepository \
            :mobile:android-filament:publishReleasePublicationToMavenCentralRepository \
            :mobile:android-firebase-ai:publishReleasePublicationToMavenCentralRepository \
            :mobile:android-detect-mlkit:publishReleasePublicationToMavenCentralRepository \
            :mobile:android-hands-androidxr:publishReleasePublicationToMavenCentralRepository \
            :mobile:android-hands-mediapipe:publishReleasePublicationToMavenCentralRepository \
            --stacktrace

  build-ios:
    name: Build Apple XCFramework
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: macos-latest
    outputs:
      checksum: ${{ steps.package_xcframework.outputs.checksum }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '20.x'

      - name: Build embedded JS engine asset
        run: |
          npm install --no-audit --no-fund
          npm run build

      - name: Set up Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@683b588c487a69d01f6c6ddf40f036ff682cc2c8 # master; stable toolchain below
        with:
          toolchain: stable
          targets: aarch64-apple-ios, aarch64-apple-ios-sim, x86_64-apple-ios, aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin

      - name: Build XCFramework
        run: bash scripts/build_ios_xcframework.sh

      - name: Verify XCFramework completeness
        run: bash scripts/verify_xcframework.sh mobile/ios/ThreeLiveCompiler.xcframework

      - name: Zip XCFramework & Compute Checksum
        id: package_xcframework
        run: |
          cd mobile/ios
          zip -r -y ThreeLiveCompiler.xcframework.zip ThreeLiveCompiler.xcframework
          CHECKSUM=$(swift package compute-checksum ThreeLiveCompiler.xcframework.zip)
          echo "XCFramework SHA-256 Checksum: ${CHECKSUM}"
          echo "checksum=${CHECKSUM}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Upload iOS XCFramework Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: ThreeLiveCompiler.xcframework.zip
          path: mobile/ios/ThreeLiveCompiler.xcframework.zip
          if-no-files-found: error


  github-release:
    name: Create GitHub Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-binaries, build-android, build-ios]
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '20.x'

      - name: Build Web JS bundles
        run: |
          npm install --no-audit --no-fund
          npm run build

      - name: Download all built artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4
        with:
          path: release-artifacts

      - name: Stage Release Assets
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist-release web-bundle/three-live web-bundle/xr-live
          find release-artifacts -type f -exec cp {} dist-release/ \;
          cp dist/*.js dist/*.min.js dist/three-live-sandbox.html web-bundle/
          cp three-live/dist/*.js three-live/dist/*.min.js three-live/dist/*.cjs three-live/dist/*.d.ts web-bundle/three-live/
          cp xr-live/dist/*.js xr-live/dist/*.min.js xr-live/dist/*.cjs xr-live/dist/*.d.ts web-bundle/xr-live/
          (cd web-bundle && zip -r ../dist-release/three-live-web-dist.zip .)
          cp dist/three-live.min.js dist/three-live-viewer.min.js dist/three-live-studio.min.js dist/three-live-cad.min.js dist/three-live-animation.min.js dist/three-live-sandbox.html dist-release/
          cp three-live/dist/three-live-full.min.js dist-release/
          cp xr-live/dist/xr-live.min.js xr-live/dist/xr-live-viewer.min.js xr-live/dist/xr-live-sensors.min.js xr-live/dist/xr-live-spatial.min.js xr-live/dist/xr-live-sim.min.js xr-live/dist/xr-live-webgpu.min.js xr-live/dist/xr-live-full.min.js dist-release/
          ls -la dist-release

      - name: Publish GitHub Release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@3bb12739c298aeb8a4eeaf626c5b8d85266b0e65 # v2
        with:
          files: dist-release/*
          body_path: CHANGELOG.md
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

  publish-npm:
    name: Publish NPM Packages
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22.x'

      - name: Install dependencies & build
        run: |
          npm install --no-audit --no-fund
          npm run build

      - name: Publish three-live monorepo packages
        env:
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "${NPM_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
            npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken "${NPM_TOKEN}"
          else
            npm install -g npm@latest || true
          fi
          for ws in three-live xr-live; do
            pkg_version="$(node -p "require('./${ws}/package.json').version")"
            if npm view "${ws}@${pkg_version}" version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "::notice::${ws}@${pkg_version} is already published on npm; skipping."
              continue
            fi
            if [ -n "${NPM_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
              npm publish --workspace="${ws}" --access public --provenance || npm publish --workspace="${ws}" --access public
            else
              npm publish --workspace="${ws}" --access public --provenance || {
                echo "::notice::npm OIDC Trusted Publishing failed for ${ws}@${pkg_version}."
                exit 0
              }
            fi
          done

  publish-mcp-registry:
    name: Publish Official MCP Registry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [publish-npm]
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Install mcp-publisher and publish server.json via GitHub OIDC
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/releases/latest/download/mcp-publisher_linux_amd64.tar.gz" | tar -xz mcp-publisher
          ./mcp-publisher validate server.json
          ./mcp-publisher login github-oidc
          ./mcp-publisher publish server.json || echo "::notice::server.json version may already be published on the Official MCP Registry."

  publish-crates:
    name: Publish Crates.io
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22.x'

      - name: Build embedded JS engine asset
        run: |
          npm install --no-audit --no-fund
          npm run build

      - name: Set up Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@683b588c487a69d01f6c6ddf40f036ff682cc2c8 # master; stable toolchain below
        with:
          toolchain: stable

      - name: Cargo Publish
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CRATES_IO_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "${CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::CRATES_IO_TOKEN secret is not configured yet; skipping crates.io publish."
            exit 0
          fi
          cargo publish --manifest-path compiler/Cargo.toml --allow-dirty || {
            echo "::notice::cargo publish exited non-zero (version may already be published on crates.io)."
            exit 0
          }

  # The SHA-256 of a release artifact cannot be known until the artifact exists, so the
  # manifest committed on the tag is necessarily stale. This pins the real values and moves
  # the tag to the corrected commit. Without this, `.binaryTarget(url:checksum:)` would keep
  # the placeholder checksum and no external consumer could resolve the package at all.
  pin-spm-manifest:
    name: Pin SPM Binary Target
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-ios, github-release]
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout tag
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Pin release tag and checksum into Package.swift
        env:
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          CHECKSUM: ${{ needs.build-ios.outputs.checksum }}
        run: bash scripts/update_spm_binary_target.sh "${TAG}" "${CHECKSUM}"

      - name: Commit, move tag, and update main
        env:
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          CHECKSUM: ${{ needs.build-ios.outputs.checksum }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if git diff --quiet -- Package.swift; then
            echo "Package.swift is already pinned for ${TAG}; nothing to do."
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add Package.swift
          git commit -m "chore: pin ThreeLiveCompiler.xcframework checksum for ${TAG}"
          git tag -f "${TAG}"
          git push --force origin "refs/tags/${TAG}"

          # Also update Package.swift on main so main carries the latest release checksum
          git fetch origin main
          git checkout -B main origin/main
          bash scripts/update_spm_binary_target.sh "${TAG}" "${CHECKSUM}"
          if ! git diff --quiet -- Package.swift; then
            git add Package.swift
            git commit -m "chore: pin ThreeLiveCompiler.xcframework checksum for ${TAG} [skip ci]"
            git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/main || echo "::warning::Could not push Package.swift update to main"
          fi

  # End-to-end proof that the published package is installable. This resolves the release
  # over the network, verifies the binary target checksum, links the XCFramework, and runs
  # the compiler -- the exact path an external user takes.
  verify-spm-consumption:
    name: Verify SPM Consumption
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [pin-spm-manifest]
    steps:
      - name: Resolve and run the published package as an external consumer
        env:
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ASSET_URL="https://github.com/google/three-live/releases/download/${TAG}/ThreeLiveCompiler.xcframework.zip"
          if ! curl -fsSLI "${ASSET_URL}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::notice::Release asset ${ASSET_URL} is not anonymously reachable yet (repository is currently private). Unauthenticated SwiftPM consumption probe will run once the repository is public."
            exit 0
          fi

          VERSION="${TAG#v}"
          WORKDIR="$(mktemp -d)"
          mkdir -p "${WORKDIR}/Sources/ConsumerProbe"
          cd "${WORKDIR}"

          cat > Sources/ConsumerProbe/main.swift <<'SWIFT'
          import Foundation
          import ThreeLiveCompiler

          let script = """
          const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(
              new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1),
              new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xffffff })
          );
          scene.add(mesh);
          """

          let glb = try ThreeCompiler.compileSync(script)
          guard Array(glb.prefix(4)) == [0x67, 0x6C, 0x54, 0x46] else {
              fatalError("Resolved package did not produce a valid GLB container")
          }
          print("Consumed ThreeLiveCompiler successfully: \(glb.count) bytes of GLB")
          SWIFT

          cat > Package.swift <<MANIFEST
          // swift-tools-version: 5.9
          import PackageDescription

          let package = Package(
              name: "ConsumerProbe",
              platforms: [.macOS(.v12)],
              dependencies: [
                  .package(url: "https://github.com/google/three-live.git", exact: "${VERSION}")
              ],
              targets: [
                  .executableTarget(
                      name: "ConsumerProbe",
                      dependencies: [.product(name: "ThreeLiveCompiler", package: "three-live")]
                  )
              ]
          )
          MANIFEST

          swift run

[package]
name = "three-live-compiler"
version = "1.4.0"
edition = "2021"
description = "High-performance procedural Three.js to binary glTF 2.0 (GLB) compiler powered by Boa"
license = "Apache-2.0"
repository = "https://github.com/google/three-live"
homepage = "https://google.github.io/three-live/"
include = [
    "src/**/*",
    "include/**/*",
    "build.rs",
    "assets/three-author-engine.min.js",
    "Cargo.toml",
]

[[bin]]
name = "three-live-cli"
path = "src/main.rs"
# `src/main.rs` uses `clap`, which is only pulled in by the `cli` feature. Without
# this, `--no-default-features` builds (e.g. wasm32) still try to compile the binary
# and fail on the missing import.
required-features = ["cli"]

[lib]
name = "three_live_compiler"
path = "src/lib.rs"
crate-type = ["rlib", "cdylib", "staticlib"]

[dependencies]
# Use enum-based JsValueInner (`jsvalue-enum`) instead of 48-bit NaN-boxing so heap
# pointers with ARM64 Top-Byte Ignore (TBI) / MTE tags on Android 11+ (`0xb400...`)
# or 5-level paging (LA57) do not trip Boa's 48-bit pointer mask assertion.
boa_engine = { version = "0.21", features = ["jsvalue-enum"] }
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0"
# Raw DEFLATE for playground scene links (`scene_link.rs`).
miniz_oxide = "0.8"
# Decodes JPEG reference images for `three_live_render --reference` (pure Rust, no rayon).
jpeg-decoder = { version = "0.3", default-features = false }
clap = { version = "4.4", features = ["derive"], optional = true }
jni = { version = "0.21", optional = true }

# Unconditional on wasm32 rather than feature-gated: `src/time.rs` needs `Date.now()`
# on that target no matter which features are selected, because
# `std::time::Instant::now()` panics there.
[target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")'.dependencies]
wasm-bindgen = "0.2"
# Transitive dependency of `boa_engine`. Since 0.3 it refuses to build for
# `wasm32-unknown-unknown` unless the top-level crate names a backend, so it has to be
# declared here even though we never call it directly. Also requires
# `RUSTFLAGS='--cfg getrandom_backend="wasm_js"'`; see `build_wasm.sh`.
getrandom = { version = "0.3", features = ["wasm_js"] }

[target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")'.dev-dependencies]
wasm-bindgen-test = "0.3"

[features]
default = ["cli"]
cli = ["dep:clap"]
# Retained as a no-op marker so existing `--features wasm` invocations keep working.
# The wasm module and its bindings are now selected by `target_arch` directly.
wasm = []
jni = ["dep:jni"]

[dev-dependencies]
serde_json = "1.0"

import com.google.mediapipe.tasks.components.containers.Category
import com.google.mediapipe.tasks.components.containers.Landmark
import com.google.threelive.HandJointSources
import com.google.threelive.XRHandGesture
import com.google.threelive.XRHandGestures
import java.util.Optional
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertNull
import org.junit.Assert.assertSame
import org.junit.Test

/** Unit tests for [MediaPipeHandJointSource] 21-landmark conversion and handedness mapping. */
class MediaPipeHandJointSourceTest {

  @Test
  fun worldLandmarksFlipYAndClassifyThumbsUpAndPinch() {
    // MediaPipe world coordinates have +Y downward, so a thumbs-up has negative Y for the thumb tip.
    val thumbsUp = MutableList(21) { Landmark.create(0f, -0.02f, 0f, Optional.empty(), Optional.empty()) }
    thumbsUp[0] = lm(0f, 0f, 0f) // WRIST
    thumbsUp[1] = lm(0f, -0.03f, 0f) // THUMB_CMC
    thumbsUp[2] = lm(0f, -0.05f, 0f) // THUMB_MCP (proximal)
    thumbsUp[3] = lm(0f, -0.10f, 0f) // THUMB_IP
    thumbsUp[4] = lm(0f, -0.16f, 0f) // THUMB_TIP (upward -> negative Y in MediaPipe)
    for (base in intArrayOf(5, 9, 13, 17)) {
      thumbsUp[base] = lm(0f, -0.05f, 0f) // MCP
      thumbsUp[base + 1] = lm(0f, -0.06f, 0f) // PIP
      thumbsUp[base + 2] = lm(0f, -0.04f, 0f) // DIP
      thumbsUp[base + 3] = lm(0f, -0.02f, 0f) // TIP (curled back toward wrist)
    }
    val joints = MediaPipeHandJointSource.fromWorldLandmarks(thumbsUp)
    assertEquals(21, joints.size)
    assertEquals(XRHandGesture.THUMBS_UP, XRHandGestures.classify(joints).gesture)
  }

  @Test
  fun handednessAndInstallRegisterSource() {
    val left = listOf(Category.create(0.95f, 0, "Left", "Left"))
    val right = listOf(Category.create(0.9f, 1, "Right", "Right"))
    assertEquals("left", MediaPipeHandJointSource.selectHandSide(left, 0))
    assertEquals("right", MediaPipeHandJointSource.selectHandSide(right, 1))
    assertEquals("right", MediaPipeHandJointSource.selectHandSide(emptyList(), 0))
    assertEquals("left", MediaPipeHandJointSource.selectHandSide(emptyList(), 1))

    val src = ThreeLiveMediaPipeHands.install()
    assertSame(src, HandJointSources.current())
    assertNull(src.joints("left"))
    HandJointSources.register(null)
  }

  private fun lm(x: Float, y: Float, z: Float): Landmark =
    Landmark.create(x, y, z, Optional.empty(), Optional.empty())
}

# Generates gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar locally.
#
# The jar is a compiled binary and is deliberately not checked in, so `./gradlew` cannot run the
# pinned Gradle version on a fresh clone. This script produces it from the version already pinned
# in gradle-wrapper.properties, and is a one-time step per clone.
#
# `gradle wrapper` also rewrites gradlew, gradlew.bat and gradle-wrapper.properties. We restore the
# checked-in versions of those afterwards so only the generated jar is left behind.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
ROOT_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"
WRAPPER_DIR="${ROOT_DIR}/gradle/wrapper"
PROPERTIES="${WRAPPER_DIR}/gradle-wrapper.properties"

if [ ! -f "${PROPERTIES}" ]; then
    echo "Error: ${PROPERTIES} not found." >&2
    exit 1
fi

GRADLE_VERSION="$(sed -n 's|.*/gradle-\([0-9][0-9.]*\)-bin\.zip.*|\1|p' "${PROPERTIES}")"
if [ -z "${GRADLE_VERSION}" ]; then
    echo "Error: could not parse the pinned Gradle version from ${PROPERTIES}." >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "=== Three-Live: generating Gradle ${GRADLE_VERSION} wrapper jar ==="

BACKUP_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${BACKUP_DIR}"' EXIT

# Fast, JVM-free extraction: every Gradle distribution bundles the standalone `gradle-wrapper.jar`
# inside `lib/plugins/gradle-wrapper-<version>.jar`. Extracting it directly via `unzip` avoids
# invoking a system/Homebrew `gradle` binary (which may run against an incompatible Java version
# such as JDK 25 before `./gradlew` is even bootstrapped).
PLUGIN_JAR="$(ls "${HOME}/.gradle/wrapper/dists/gradle-${GRADLE_VERSION}"-*/*/gradle-"${GRADLE_VERSION}"/lib/plugins/gradle-wrapper-"${GRADLE_VERSION}".jar 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)"
if [ -z "${PLUGIN_JAR}" ]; then
    PLUGIN_JAR="$(ls "${HOME}/.gradle/wrapper/dists"/gradle-*-*/*/gradle-*/lib/plugins/gradle-wrapper-*.jar 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1 || true)"
fi

if [ -z "${PLUGIN_JAR}" ] || [ ! -f "${PLUGIN_JAR}" ]; then
    echo "--> Downloading Gradle ${GRADLE_VERSION} distribution to extract gradle-wrapper.jar..."
    curl -fsSL "https://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-${GRADLE_VERSION}-bin.zip" -o "${BACKUP_DIR}/gradle.zip"
    unzip -qo "${BACKUP_DIR}/gradle.zip" "gradle-${GRADLE_VERSION}/lib/plugins/gradle-wrapper-${GRADLE_VERSION}.jar" -d "${BACKUP_DIR}"
    PLUGIN_JAR="${BACKUP_DIR}/gradle-${GRADLE_VERSION}/lib/plugins/gradle-wrapper-${GRADLE_VERSION}.jar"
fi

mkdir -p "${WRAPPER_DIR}"
unzip -p "${PLUGIN_JAR}" gradle-wrapper.jar > "${WRAPPER_DIR}/gradle-wrapper.jar"
chmod +x "${ROOT_DIR}/gradlew"

if [ ! -f "${WRAPPER_DIR}/gradle-wrapper.jar" ]; then
    echo "Error: gradle wrapper ran but produced no jar." >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "=== Done. './gradlew' now runs Gradle ${GRADLE_VERSION}. ==="
echo "Note: gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar is gitignored and must not be committed."
